This would break down with nested url tags: `[url=https://example.com/t]Test [url]https://example.com[/url][/url]`
But I think it's fine to ignore this edge case, if there is no easy solution.

Since we remove those anyway, could we maybe move this to the general replacements above? I'd imagine it's not uncommon to use `font` and `color` over multiple lines so always removing those closing tags would account for that.

At the moment we don't handle escaping of special markdown characters anywhere. But at least for [ and ] it would make sense to escape them (the markdown way) since they are special characters in markdown as well.
This has to happen before URLs or the url content will be converted to inline code.
Nitpick: Casing of code block should be consistent. Either use `codeblock` everywhere of use `code_block` everywhere.

An issue is that what works in VSCode causes issues in Zed and vice versa currently. Zed does not process trailing backslashes or double spaces as line breaks: the only thing it processes as line breaks is \n (which to my understanding it shouldn't at all but that's just how it is from testing currently) I've tried: - `
` - `
` - `\\` (one backslash) - `\\ ` (one backslash and two trailing spaces) - ` ` (two trailing spaces) And combinations of these four with `\n`s. The issue in Zed is it'll just leave the backslash or any characters other than `\n` as-is. How about turning Godot's `[br]`s into markdown paragraphs (`\n\n`)? Right now it's the only thing that works across the two editors for me.

For this, one option would be to change the algorithm to never search and replace many times over entire lines but to advance the cursor each time something is replaced:

- Find [, find the nearest ]
- Apply all the rules between brackets
- As soon as a match/rule is met, replace and advance to the first character after ]
- Repeat the operation

This is generally a bit more reliable/less prone to edge cases than the current approach of going over the entire line multiple times.

Any thoughts on that?

This is where a parser would start to become necessary.

I'd ignore this mainly because the use case is narrow, and consider addressing it if it becomes an issue in practice for users.
Zed certainly supports `\\\n` (one backslash and one newline)
Yeah totally fine :+1:

Ah I see! You make sure every \n is preceded with a \\. Great, thanks, let's use that then! I was not touching the existing \n in the input strings which was likely the cause of failures, which makes sense now.

When doing inline element parsing like list items `\\\n` doesn't work, a literal \ ends up being inserted. Same issue if this is trailing at the end of the string (both in VSCode and Zed). I'll make sure to document that in the code.
Might be leading spaces :thinking:

But well, it's no big deal, if a simple line break doesn't work I'll just use a paragraph break as you did. Since Godot 4 GDScript supports unicode identifiers. We should use the unicode identifier groups here. We have the methods `is_unicode_identifier_continue` and `is_unicode_identifier_start` for that. (With those `url` would be a valid class name, but I think it's fine to just add a check `content != "url"` here.)
